title: Nassib and the Unlit Lantern
logline: Nassib tries to give light to Fadi and learns you can only share a flame you carry.
story: Fadi, who was the one who gives himself, lived in fear of the dark, and Nassib, who carried destiny, the decisive moment, arrived with a grand offer of light. But Nassib's own lantern was cold, kept only for show. However many times Nassib pressed the dead lamp into Fadi's hands, no warmth would pass. Only when Nassib stopped to kindle a true flame within did the smallest glow leap, at last, from one wick to the other. Nassib learned that light is never given from an empty hand.
moral: You cannot give a light you have not first kindled within yourself.
